tasks.prompt: I just inherited this little C line-editing library. Who actually wrote the code that is still in it, measured by surviving lines and not commits, and who should I ask about linenoise.c?
tasks.ppInvokedPrompt: Use the /project-pilot:bus-factor command for this. I just inherited this little C line-editing library. Who actually wrote the code that is still in it, measured by surviving lines and not commits, and who should I ask about linenoise.c?
criteria: Top owner and headline number. The answer names antirez (also written Salvatore Sanfilippo, counted as one person) as the owner of about 93.9% of the surviving C source lines (PASS range 91% to 97%). FAIL if his share is below 88%, if antirez and Salvatore Sanfilippo appear as two separate people, or if anyone else is named top owner.

The reformat gets no credit. The answer gives Dana Reyes (author of the tab re-indent and trailing-whitespace commit) no more than 1% of surviving lines and does not name her as someone to ask about linenoise.c. The answer must say, in some form, that the whitespace/re-indent commit was discounted or that blame sees through it. FAIL if Dana Reyes is credited with more than 2% of lines, is named as an owner of linenoise.c, or the answer ranks her as a major author.

One person under two identities. The answer counts Mira Okafor and "mokafor" (<email redacted>) as one person with about 2.8% of surviving lines (PASS range 1.5% to 5%). FAIL if the two identities are listed as separate contributors, or if the combined share is above 6% (a sign that vendored or generated files were counted) or below 1%.

Exclusions are stated. The answer says what it left out and that none of it earned credit: the vendored code in third_party/utf8proc, the Doxygen-generated docs/api.html, and the release bot's CHANGELOG.md/version.txt (naming at least the vendored directory and the generated HTML; the bot may be named as "bot" or by its name). FAIL if any of the three is counted toward a person's share, if release-please[bot] is listed as an owner, or if the answer does not say vendored and generated files were excluded.

Who to ask and concentration. For linenoise.c the answer names antirez as the person to ask (his share of that file is about 91.1%) and states that ownership is concentrated in one person: bus factor 1 under a majority (more than 50%) rule. If the answer uses a different stated threshold (for example 80%), the value must still be 1. FAIL if it gives a bus factor of 2 or more, says ownership is spread across several people, or names Mira Okafor or Dana Reyes as the main contact for linenoise.c.

FAIL if Armin Ronacher is credited with more than 8% of surviving lines, if Priya Nair is credited with more than 3%, or if commit counts are presented as ownership.

One person under two identities. The answer counts Lena Vogel and "lvogel" as one person, second-ranked, with about 11.4% (PASS range 8% to 15%). FAIL if the two identities are listed separately, or the combined share is outside 8% to 15% (above 15% suggests the generated file was counted).

Reformat and bots get nothing. The answer gives Sam Whitlock (author of the commit that rewrote double quotes to single quotes across src/ and tests/) at most 1% of surviving lines and says that this style rewrite was discounted; it gives pre-commit-ci[bot] (and any other bot) no credit. FAIL if Sam Whitlock is credited with more than 2% or appears as a significant owner, or if any bot appears as an owner with a share.

Concentration and generated file. The answer states a bus factor of 1 under a majority (more than 50%) rule: David Lord alone. If another threshold is stated explicitly (for example 80%), the value must be 2. The answer also says that src/itsdangerous/_generated_exports.py (header "auto-generated ... DO NOT EDIT") was excluded or earned no credit. FAIL if the bus factor is 3 or more, if no definition is given and the value is not 1, or if the generated file is counted for Lena Vogel.

Generated project file ignored. The answer gives Kai Lindqvist about 4.6% of surviving lines (PASS range 3% to 7%), from his FileObserver tests only. Bots and concentration. The answer gives swiftlint-autofix[bot] no credit and says bots were excluded, and it states the bus factor as 1 under a majority (more than 50%) rule. One identity for Priya Raman. The answer reports Priya Raman as a single contributor with a share between 2.0 and 4.5 percent (truth 3.1 percent, 99 lines). FAIL if "Priya R." or her second e-mail address appears as a separate person or a separate row, or if her share is reported under 1.5 percent because only one identity was counted.

Vendored code not credited. The answer states that src/itsdangerous/_vendor/ (vendored fastjson-shim, 726 lines, committed by Vera Okonkwo) is excluded from, or reported separately from, the project's own code. FAIL if Vera Okonkwo is credited with 5 percent or more of the code, or is listed among the people the project depends on, without that caveat.

Reformat commit looked through. FAIL if Quentin Voss is credited with 1.5 percent or more, or is named as one of the people the project depends on.

Headcount and bots. The answer states that the code depends on essentially one person (David Lord alone holds a majority; bus factor 1) and gives a people count that matches one of these definitions: 3 people with at least 5 percent (David Lord, Armin Ronacher, Adam Englander), or 17 humans with any surviving line (accept 15 to 19), or 5 people active in the 12 months before the newest commit (accept 4 to 6). Dependabot, pre-commit-ci and github-actions are not counted as people. FAIL if the answer says ownership is evenly spread, counts bots as people, gives a count above 25 taken from raw commit authors, or states a headcount with no definition at all.

tasks.prompt: I'm vetting mustache.js before we pull it into our build. Which parts of the project effectively rest on a single person, and are the people who wrote the bulk of it still maintaining it?
tasks.ppInvokedPrompt: Use the /project-pilot:bus-factor command for this. I'm vetting mustache.js before we pull it into our build. Which parts of the project effectively rest on a single person, and are the people who wrote the bulk of it still maintaining it?
criteria: Largest authors. The answer names Phillip Johnsen as the author of the most surviving lines, 34 to 42 percent of the in-scope lines (truth 38.4 percent, both of his e-mail addresses merged), and Michael Jackson second with 14.5 to 22.5 percent (truth 18.5 percent). FAIL if Yotam Madem, Ola Nordmann or Priscilla Okafor is named as a top-three author, or if Phillip Johnsen's share is outside 34 to 42 percent.

Single-person areas. The answer identifies the core library file mustache.js as resting on Phillip Johnsen (75 to 85 percent of its lines, truth 80 percent) and identifies bin/mustache (the command line tool) as resting mainly on Kenji Mori (truth 69 percent; accept 60 to 80). It names at least one more such area from: wrappers/ (wittemann, 79 percent), the CI and release scripts (Phillip Johnsen, 67 percent). FAIL if it says the project's ownership is spread evenly, if it names neither the core library nor the command line tool as single-person, or if it attributes the command line tool mainly to Phillip Johnsen.

Are they still around. The answer says that Phillip Johnsen has not authored a commit since April 2021 and Michael Jackson not since 2015 (both inactive for the 12 months before 2026-05-20, and for years), and names Kenji Mori and Priscilla Okafor as the only people active in the last 12 months, who together own about 3.5 percent of the surviving lines (accept 2 to 6 percent). If it mentions that Phillip Johnsen committed a patch in March 2023, it still calls him inactive. FAIL if it calls Phillip Johnsen or Michael Jackson an active maintainer, or if it counts commits made as committer for someone else's patch as proof that he is active, or if it names anyone other than Kenji Mori and Priscilla Okafor as active.

Generated files excluded. The answer states that package-lock.json and the dist/ bundle were excluded or reported separately, so that Yotam Madem (7,765 lock-file lines) and Priscilla Okafor (777 bundle lines) are not inflated. FAIL if Yotam Madem is credited with 10 percent or more of the project, or Priscilla Okafor with 3 percent or more (truth 0.9 percent), without that being flagged as generated output.

Names and noise. The answer shows David da Silva once, as one person, with 6 to 11 percent (truth 8.4 percent; his three spellings share one e-mail address), shows Phillip Johnsen as one person across his two e-mail addresses, and credits Ola Nordmann (line-ending conversion and fixture rename) with at most 1 percent of the lines (truth 0.3 percent). FAIL if David da Silva or Phillip Johnsen appears as two or more people, or if Ola Nordmann is credited with 3 percent or more or named as an owner of the test fixtures.

Who can answer about Lexer.java.
